title: Keep the workspace's inherit flag when a consent switch changes
request: The owner: fix the bug a reviewer found while mapping the team's switch: changing a workspace consent switch dropped the flag that gives new projects the workspace's switches.
spec: dclab_rnd/consent.py (the workspace's consent file; decision 6 of the phases 4-5 plan, package 27.2)
plan: Write a test that sets the inherit flag, changes the switches, and reads the flag back.
Make every writer of the consent file change only its own keys and keep the rest.

decisions.decision: One function changes the consent file's keys under a process lock, and both writers use it.
decisions.why: Each writer read the file and wrote back only what it knew; the switch's writer knew only the two switches, so it dropped the inherit flag, and two writers at once could drop each other's change.

change: dclab_rnd/consent.py (_update; set_workspace_consent and set_inherits through it); tests/test_consent.py (WorkspaceSwitchTest).

findings.defect: Changing a workspace consent switch dropped the projects_inherit flag.
findings.scenario: The owner set new projects to inherit the workspace's switches, then turned on training consent: the file was rewritten with the two switches only, and new projects no longer inherited them.
findings.cause: The switch's writer rebuilt the file from the two switches it reads, not from the file.
findings.fix: Every writer reads the whole file, changes its own keys and writes it back atomically, one at a time in the process.

outcome: Changing a consent switch keeps the inherit flag and every other key of the workspace's consent file.
lessons: A settings file written by more than one function needs one writer that changes keys, not whole files.
